summary: @factiii/runner: disclosed remote-agent CLI pairs over WebRTC and executes shell/agent commands on the host
details: @factiii/runner is a daemon started by the user via `factiii-runner start` that pairs with Factiii web and mobile clients over WebRTC (signaled through api.factiii.com) and executes AI-agent commands (claude, codex, shell) on the host. In dist/cli.js, WebRTC data channel handlers (setRemoteDescription, DataChannel) feed received messages into child_process spawn/exec and child.stdin.write, so the paired remote peer drives process execution on the installer's machine. The tarball also ships frpc reverse-tunnel binaries under vendor/frpc-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64}. Pairing is gated by a JWT stored encrypted at ~/.factiii-runner/config.json and provisioned through a browser login flow, so unpaired peers cannot drive the shell. The remote-execution capability, the WebRTC pairing, and the agent-driven shell are the documented product behavior described in the README. The daemon is user-invoked (no install-time or import-time lifecycle hook starts it), does not harvest installer secrets outside of its own config, and contacts only Factiii-controlled infrastructure. The full-host blast radius (arbitrary command execution under the user's account, plus bundled reverse-tunnel binaries) is a material trust decision for anyone installing it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
